name: What if my ADU needs a second story?

mainEntity.name: What if my ADU needs a second story because the lot is too small for a one-story layout?
mainEntity.text: What if my ADU needs a second story because the lot is too small for a one-story layout?

acceptedAnswer.text: A second-story ADU is sometimes the best answer on small or narrow lots, especially when the owner wants to preserve yard space. The tradeoff is higher complexity: the structure must support the added load, stairs must be designed efficiently, and privacy impacts on neighboring homes must be considered. A two-story solution may also trigger more careful review of height, massing, and fire separation. In some cases, a second level makes sense only if the ground floor can be kept compact or dedicated to parking, storage, or entry functions. A good design team will compare a one-story and two-story option side by side, including cost, square footage, privacy, and outdoor space. Homeowners should be cautious about adding a second floor just to gain area if the site can achieve the same function with a simpler footprint. The structural and permitting burden can outweigh the benefit unless the lot truly demands it.
acceptedAnswer.description: A second-story ADU can solve a tight-lot problem, but it adds structural cost, privacy concerns, stair design, and potential height-limit challenges. It works best when the site can support the structure and when the layout justifies the extra complexity.
